newsitem.title: JAPAN: SHOWA CDU TO BE SHUT AT LEAST 10 DAYS--FIRE DEPT.
newsitem.headline: SHOWA CDU TO BE SHUT AT LEAST 10 DAYS--FIRE DEPT.

text.p: Showa Yokkaichi Sekiyu Co Ltd's 150,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) in central Japan, which was hit by a fire on Monday, must stay closed for at least 10 days, a fire department official said on Tuesday.

"It really depends on the cause of the fire. But it will take at least 10 days or so to go through all the procedures that are necessary to lift the suspension order," an official at a local fire department said.
The fire broke out on Monday afternoon when heated residue oil leaked from a pipe extending from the CDU and caught fire.
The leakage occurred when workers were checking a device measuring the flow of oil in the pipe, a plant spokesman said. Four workers were injured.
The fire department suspended operations of the unit immediately after the fire, and is currently investigating the cause of the accident.
Showa Yokkaichi, which belongs to the Showa Shell Sekiyu KK group, will compensate for the expected loss in production by securing oil products from other group refineries, the spokesman said.
The plant's other CDU, with a crude processing capacity of 90,000 bpd, is running normally, he added.
Showa Shell Sekiyu, an oil refiner and distributor, is owned 50 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group
